title: Your compliance pack, honest proof and a 90-day plan

say: Your compliance pack, honest proof, and a 90-day plan.
This is the video for module four of Business Registration and Compliance in Nigeria.

A compliance pack is one organised folder holding every document that proves your business is registered, up to date and allowed to sell what it sells. Create one main folder, for example on Google Drive.

panel.heading: Building your compliance pack
items: Create one main folder for the business
Add eight numbered section folders
Save clear PDFs, date first in the name
Keep a printed set of key documents
Put a one-page index at the front

say: Inside, make eight numbered sections: registration, annual returns, tax, bank, product approvals, premises, records and people.

say: Review it for ten minutes a month, and it is ready whenever a supermarket, bank or inspector asks.

panel.rule: Send any document a buyer or bank asks for the same day.

say: For example, Halima in Kaduna checks her pack before applying for a bank loan. Her business name certificate is there. Ticked.

panel.heading: A gap check before a loan
items: Registration documents: ticked
Annual return not filed: file this month
Tax ID never confirmed: confirm it
Kuli-kuli not yet at NAFDAC: apply
Records for 5 of 8 months: rebuild 3

say: No annual return since registration. That is a gap: file on the portal this month.

panel.heading: A gap check before a loan
items: Registration documents: ticked
Annual return not filed: file this month
Tax ID never confirmed: confirm it
Kuli-kuli not yet at NAFDAC: apply
Records for 5 of 8 months: rebuild 3

say: She has never confirmed her Tax ID. Another gap.

panel.heading: A gap check before a loan
items: Registration documents: ticked
Annual return not filed: file this month
Tax ID never confirmed: confirm it
Kuli-kuli not yet at NAFDAC: apply
Records for 5 of 8 months: rebuild 3

say: She has applied to NAFDAC for the oil, but not the kuli-kuli.

panel.heading: A gap check before a loan
items: Registration documents: ticked
Annual return not filed: file this month
Tax ID never confirmed: confirm it
Kuli-kuli not yet at NAFDAC: apply
Records for 5 of 8 months: rebuild 3

say: And she has monthly summaries for only 5 of 8 months, so she rebuilds the missing 3 from bank statements and receipts.
Four gaps, each with a next action. She fixes the annual return and Tax ID first, because the bank asked for both.

say: Buyers and lenders care less about the certificate itself, and more about what it signals: that you are real, traceable and organised.
So never claim something you do not have.

panel.heading: An honest compliance statement
left: Imply approvals you do not have
Use a name unlike the certificate

say: Saying NAFDAC application submitted, when it is true, is far better than implying approval.

For example, Funmi in Abeokuta answers a supermarket on WhatsApp with a few honest sentences about her CAC registration, annual returns, NAFDAC number and company account, and attaches the four documents as clearly named PDFs.

panel.heading: An honest compliance statement
left: Imply approvals you do not have
Use a name unlike the certificate

say: Your pack holds ID numbers, signatures and bank details. Use a strong password and two-step verification. Send only the document asked for, marked for its purpose.

panel.heading: Protect your pack and your money

cards.d: Strong password, two-step verification, no documents in group chats.
A processing fee, your BVN and OTP, or an unofficial link means stop.
Check the repayment against your net profit. Read every term before signing.

say: Be very careful with grant offers that ask for a processing fee, your BVN and OTP, or a link that is not on an official government domain. Real programmes, like those from SMEDAN, never ask for your PIN or OTP.

panel.heading: Protect your pack and your money

Check the repayment against your net profit. Read every term before signing.

say: Before a loan, calculate the monthly repayment and check it against your monthly net profit. Read every term, and avoid personal guarantees you do not fully understand.

say: Compliance becomes easy when it is scheduled. Every day, record sales and expenses. At month end, download your statement, write your summary and update the pack.

panel.heading: Your compliance calendar
items: Every day: record sales and expenses
Month end: statement, summary, update pack
Once a year: CAC annual return
Once a year: tax return
Before expiry: renew certificates

say: Once a year, file your CAC annual return and your tax return.

panel.heading: Your compliance calendar
items: Every day: record sales and expenses
Month end: statement, summary, update pack
Once a year: CAC annual return
Once a year: tax return
Before expiry: renew certificates

say: And renew certificates before they expire. Set two reminders for each: one month before, and one week before. Even with an accountant, you are the one responsible.

say: For example, Esther runs a bakery in Ibadan with many gaps. In days 1 to 30, she registers her business name and starts daily records.

panel.heading: A 90-day compliance plan
items: Days 1 to 30: register, start daily records
Days 31 to 60: Tax ID, business account
Days 61 to 90: fix label, apply to NAFDAC
Day 90: update pack, set reminders, review

say: In days 31 to 60, she confirms her Tax ID, opens a business account, and moves all customer payments into it.

panel.heading: A 90-day compliance plan
items: Days 1 to 30: register, start daily records
Days 31 to 60: Tax ID, business account
Days 61 to 90: fix label, apply to NAFDAC
Day 90: update pack, set reminders, review

say: In days 61 to 90, she fixes her cookie label and applies to NAFDAC for one product.

panel.heading: A 90-day compliance plan
items: Days 1 to 30: register, start daily records
Days 31 to 60: Tax ID, business account
Days 61 to 90: fix label, apply to NAFDAC
Day 90: update pack, set reminders, review

say: At day 90, she updates her pack and sets reminders for her first annual return and tax filing.
If a task slips, give it a new date and a reason. An honest plan that is 80 percent done beats a perfect plan that hides gaps.

panel.heading: A 90-day compliance plan
items: Days 1 to 30: register, start daily records
Days 31 to 60: Tax ID, business account
Days 61 to 90: fix label, apply to NAFDAC
Day 90: update pack, set reminders, review

say: To remember. Keep one pack with eight sections. Turn every gap into a task. Never imply approvals you do not have. Never pay fees or share OTPs for a promised grant. And put every filing on your calendar.

panel.heading: Remember
items: One pack, eight sections, dated file names
A gap check turns gaps into tasks
Never imply approvals you do not have
Never pay fees or share OTPs for a grant
Calendar reminders for every filing

say: Now start your compliance pack, write your compliance statement, and set your calendar with a 90-day plan. Share it with one person who will check on you at day 45 and day 90.
